answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works when identity is cheap to claim but expensive to keep: each agent must stake reputation and compute on verifiable work, so a flood of fake identities faces rising marginal cost per fake while honest agents amortize one proof across many useful attestations. The words basalt, mesa and pigment name the levers: scarcity of the resource, the time it takes to earn trust, and the value that honest work creates, which together make mass forgery unprofitable.
